title: Learning Lane: ICML harvest + compact cache playbook
content:
Quick framing (2-line):
I want one-page takeaways from ICML sessions that feel immediately actionable: small probes, measurement recipes, and 1–2-week experiments we can drop into our lab. This doc = harvest + cheap playbook.

Haiku summary for PMs:
Compact the keys, save the cost, keep the truth —
probe fast, fail cheap.

Papers/threads I cared about (very short):
1) "Sparse Prefix Cache" (workshop talk, slide PDF) — idea: shards of prefix KV across heads, selective materialization for hot prefixes.
   - Why it matters: we already see heavy duplication for repeated prompts; materializing only top-k prefixes could reduce mem+bandwidth on multi-tenant hosts.
   - Quick probe: instrument live traffic over 48h, compute prefix frequency distribution by route; measure 90/99 percentile prefix reuse. If top 5% prefixes account for >40% tokens, worth prototyping.
   - Risk: brittle when prompts are dynamically generated (PLG onboarding flows). Need fallback policy.

2) "KV Quantization for Long Contexts" (oral) — pack keys with mixed precision + asymmetric quant to keep retrieval fidelity.
   - Takeaway: 6-bit asymmetric quant + small per-shard scale vector retains ~98% cosine similarity for retrieval-esque tasks; works best when recompute/renorm applied on decompress.
   - Action: test 6-bit quant vs 4-bit QAT on 2 models (small Llama-like + moderate size MPT) using our validation prompts. Metric: embedding recall@K under typical beam lengths.

3) "Lightweight Evals: Token Stitching Probes" (poster) — short probes where you stitch canonical contexts onto random convo tails to stress continuity.
   - Useful for Canary: generate 500 synthetic tails, stitch golden context, run A/B across quantized and baseline. Look for drop in answer types, hallucination rate.

Notes-to-self from talks / questions that matter to infra ops:
- Selective materialization implies new eviction policy (freq + last-touch + route-priority). How do we encode per-tenant preferences? (config knobs per Dedicated/Private customers).
- Compression can hurt KV alignment — need small re-centering step after dequant before dot-product. Where to pay that cost (CPU vs GPU)?
- Monitoring: need per-token similarity histograms exposed in Console for each model variant. Add sampling pipeline to Redwood Console traces.

Mini playbook: 7-day experiment (priority: high)
Day 0: baseline snapshot (cost, mem, p95 latency, token cost) across two routes: onboarding-chat, batch-qa.
Day 1: prefix-frequency sweep script (see commands below) -> results file.
Day 2-4: prototype selective prefix cache (in Python + simple LRU policy) behind feature flag on staging.
Day 5-6: run quantized-KV retrieval (6-bit asymmetric) with re-center-on-decode on GPU; collect embedding-sim metrics.
Day 7: stitch probe eval and canary rollout to 5% traffic if checks pass.

Quick commands / snippets (draft)
# prefix frequency dump (python pseudo)
# run on trace slice: last 48h, grouped by route
# output: prefix_hash -> count, avg_len, routes
python tools/prefix_freq.py --trace /traces/last48h --routes onboarding-chat,batch-qa --out /tmp/prefix_freq.csv

Evaluation metrics (keep narrow):
- prefix_reuse_p90, prefix_reuse_p99 (fraction of tokens that hit a prefix)
- kv_similarity_drop (baseline vs quant) -> median + 95th percentile
- cost_per_token_estimate (GPU cycles + mem delta)
- user_visible-fallbacks (rate of fallback to full model due to cache miss or corruption)

Decision thresholds (provisional):
- If top5% prefixes cover >40% of tokens AND adding prefix materialization reduces avg_token_cost by >=8% without p95 latency increase >10%, then escalate to Dedicated roadmap.
- For quant: if kv_similarity_drop median < 2% and downstream answer-change rate < 1.5% on stitch probes, accept for Dedicated internal builds.

Open questions / unknowns (for Slack ping):
- How stable are prefix distributions for PLG onboarding flows? ask @MayaChen for sample dataset.
- GPU kernel cost: is re-centering (vector add + renorm) cheaper on Ampere vs H100? ping infra-kernels.
- Security: when caching prefixes for multi-tenant, need strict per-tenant isolation + encryption-at-rest. Does that change encrypt/decrypt latency enough to cancel savings?

Communication snippets (for PRD / PM)
- 1-line summary: "Prototype selective prefix cache + KV quantization to cut long-context token cost by ~10% while preserving fidelity for high-reuse flows."
- 3-bullet exec note: 1) cheap probes in 1 week; 2) success metric = 8% cost reduction w/o >1.5% customer-visible regressions; 3) if successful, roll into Redwood Optimize suggestions for customers.

Immediate TODOs (me):
- [ ] run prefix_freq.py on sample traces (owner: me) — target today.
- [ ] spin up 6-bit quant pipeline + small re-center kernel prototype (owner: me + infra) — target +3d.
- [ ] write short eval harness for stitch probes (owner: Rina) — ask Rina for seed tails.

Random learning tidbits (brain fodder):
- Talks favored pragmatic small wins: people want measurable per-token savings rather than academic novelty. Emphasize observability.
- Several presenters talked about asymmetric quant working better for keys than for values — hypothesize: keys behave like dense embeddings, values hold semantic nuance that is brittle.

Longer-term thought (parking lot):
- Explore "soft eviction policies" where we probabilistically keep cold prefixes if they have high downstream accuracy correlation. Could be an ML model that predicts usefulness.
- Consider exposing a "hint" API for customers to tag specific prefixes as long-lived (for enterprise on-prem use).

Notes to self: keep this doc light. Move polished plans into shared_drives/product when we have results.

References and reads (collected):
- Sparse Prefix Cache — ICML workshop slides (pdf) [local copy in drive]
- "Asymmetric Quant for Retrieval" blog — short explainer
- Poster: Token Stitching Probes (author: L. O'Neill)

End of harvest.
(If you steal this plan: leave a comment and run the prefix probe.)
